issue_context.title: k8s liveness probe fails during pod termination
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I've tested with k8s v1.21 on Amazon EKS and k8s v1.22, v1.21, and v1.20 in Minikube

I installed a pod containing a simple http server having some `/alive` endpoint.  In the pod spec, specify a liveness probe that uses this endpoint.
No liveness probe failure while pod is running, as expected.
But after executing a `kubectl delete po` command, will see k8s event that liveness probe failed.

I can reliably reproduce this.  tried with servers written in spring boot, golang, and python/gunicorn


Then I modified the server, added a second endpoint `/slow` that sleeps for 30 seconds
I call this endpoint, then immediately execute `kubectl delete po` then `kubectl get po -o yaml`
Can see that deletionTimestamp is now non-null, but liveness probe continually fails while app spends 30 seconds trying to shut-down

Starting minikube command `minikube start --extra-config=kubelet.v=4`, I never see log `Pod deletion requested, setting probe result to success` from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.21.0/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go#L234



### What did you expect to happen?

Based on [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.21.0/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go#L233) logic, I would expect liveness probe not to fail during shutdown

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Install a pod containing an http server.  Server should expose an endpoint that's used by livenessProbe in the Pod spec
Delete the pod.
Now, execute `kubectl get events`, see the liveness probe failure event(s)

for example,

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-server
spec:
  containers:
    - name: test-server
      image: waltersmatthew/goserver:latest
      ports:
        - name: http
          containerPort: 8080
          protocol: TCP
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /alive
          port: http
        periodSeconds: 1
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

1.21.0, 1.21.2 among others

### Cloud provider

AWS EKS, minikube

From this pr:https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/98571, Stop probing a pod during graceful shutdown was added, but it only takes effect while kubelet first sees the pod which was deleted(with deletionTimestamp) early, because the probe manager always holds the pod when it was first added by `HandPodAddition `, would not be changed after.  so you execute `kubectl delete po`, the probemanager could not see the pod.deletionTimestamp. /cc @matthyx

> the probe manager always holds the pod when it was first added by `HandPodAddition `, would not be changed after

@249043822 could you elaborate ? I don't think I understand what you mean.

> > the probe manager always holds the pod when it was first added by `HandPodAddition `, would not be changed after
> 
> @249043822 could you elaborate ? I don't think I understand what you mean.

Sorry @matthyx , I meant that while executing ` kubectl delete po` command, actually the probe manager could not perceive that the pod is deleted, because the variable w.pod in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cb303e613a121a29364f75cc67d3d580833a7479/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go#L233 was set while the pod was creating(as calling probeMananger.AddPod(pod)https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cb303e613a121a29364f75cc67d3d580833a7479/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2116), but w.pod could not be refreshed again since then, that's the reason for this issue. do you think so?

Hmm, not quite, because the pod is updated by reconciliation:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a0dfd958d5c5e8c2bd5fd30e1d2e9031e9aba1b6/pkg/kubelet/config/config.go#L420

I think @249043822  means:  

- when pods being added from a config source, execute kl.probeManager.AddPod(pod), start liveness probeManager worker

1. When starting probeManager worker, if `pod.ObjectMeta.DeletionTimestamp != nil`, then meet the conditions `if w.pod.ObjectMeta.DeletionTimestamp != nil && (w.probeType == liveness || w.probeType == startup) {` in `kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go`
2. Otherwise, if the probeManager worker is started, the pod.ObjectMeta.DeletionTimestamp information in the worker will be nil, and the information in probeManager  worker will not be updated, always nil. 

- So this  explains the doubt ,I think this is reasonable

Do you think so, @matthyx ?

It is updated... trust me. Pod graceful shutdown is something covered in several e2e tests.

The only question is whether this update is fast enough for this use case.

> The only question is whether this update is fast enough for this use case.

I should have mentioned that deploying a pod on its own is just the minimal example to reproduce.
In reality I see the issue while doing a rolling upgrades of k8s deployments.  But, I've noticed that when upgrading a deployment, on average, only about 15-20% of the currently running pods fail the liveness check during shutdown.

During my testing, I also experienced this while upgrading a DaemonSet, again it was about 15-20% of the pods that failed the liveness probe during shutdown.

Copying some notes from the PR:

There's an overlapping change that needs to be made before this will be totally correct (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105014) - you can't rely on the pod manager to correctly indicate whether a pod "has terminated", because the pod manager just tracks desired pods, not "pods the kubelet is running".

However, even after that change the PR may not be a completely safe change, because a pod that has defined a liveness probe AND expects a long grace period may specify a shorter termination period for liveness failures (i.e. a container that may take 10 minutes to clean up is allowed to define a liveness probe that if fails, shuts the pod down in 10 seconds).  For more detail on that, see 

    kubectl explain deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.livenessProbe.terminationGracePeriodSeconds

The contract is that a liveness probe and readiness probe can run during shutdown, and only certain probes know which container is honoring them (specifically only exec definitely targets one container).  We might want to stop probes when each container stops, but some probes can have side effects that might be broken if we stop containers early.  So our best option might be to have the probe failure squelched if the specific container is already stopped (which would hide the notification mentioned in the issue).  But that might also have some side effects if we add additional CRI calls in that path to check the container status (which would be necessary to be certain the container is stopped vs hung).

review_comments: Yeah, the configsource always sends a copy of the pod to config source channel,so we added podManager here.

There's an overlapping change that needs to be made before this will be totally correct - you can't rely on the pod manager to correctly indicate whether a pod "has terminated", because the pod manager just tracks desired pods, not "pods the kubelet is running".

There is a separate change https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105014 that probably needs to be done before this merges to more correctly take into account how pod lifecycle must handle probes.

However, even after that change this may not be the correct behavior, because a pod that has defined a liveness probe AND expects a long grace period may specify a shorter termination period for liveness failures (i.e. a container that may take 10 minutes to clean up is allowed to define a liveness probe that if fails, shuts the pod down in 10 seconds).  For more detail on that, see 

    kubectl explain deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.livenessProbe.terminationGracePeriodSeconds

The contract is that a liveness probe and readiness probe can run during shutdown, and only certain probes know which container is honoring them.  We might want to stop probes when each container stops, but some probes can have side effects that might be broken if we stop containers early.

This change that relies on pod manager is only to indicate whether a pod "has deleted",  not "has terminated".
As the housekeeping still would shutdown probes for undesired pods, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/40c2d049465417f510e4182b05953a49fc5693d4/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1106

Actually if we consider the feature ProbeTerminationGracePeriod, this logic above for probe is not correct, I just want to fix that bug https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/107473 at that time. Now I think these codes may be not useful, actually from our tests, the probes for terminating(deteted) pod are basically always shutted down by housekeeping, the codes above have no chance to run.
